# `e2e-v1` test vector

`e2e-vector.json` is generated by `remote::e2e::tests::published_vector_matches`
(`ORKESTR_WRITE_E2E_VECTOR=1 cargo test -p orkestr-core --lib remote::e2e`) and
checked byte-for-byte by the same test. It has also been verified with WebCrypto
(Node 24): signatures, ECDH, HKDF and both records.

Encoding: binary values are base64url **without padding**; public keys are raw
SEC1 uncompressed P-256 (65 bytes); private keys are the raw 32-byte scalar
(use as JWK `d`); signatures are ECDSA P-256/SHA-256 in P1363 form (64 bytes).
Rust signatures are RFC 6979 deterministic; WebCrypto ones are randomized, so
a TS implementation must *verify* `serverHello.sig` / `clientFinish.sig`, not
compare its own signatures.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `coreId`, `deviceId` | UTF-8 strings mixed into transcript and HKDF info |
| `ts` | `clientHello.ts`, unix **milliseconds**, encoded `u64` big-endian in the transcript |
| `cikPrivate` / `cikPublic` | Core identity key (signs `serverHello`) |
| `devicePrivate` / `devicePublic` | Device key DK (signs `clientFinish`) |
| `ephDPrivate` / `ephDPublic`, `nonceD` | Device ephemeral ECDH key and 32-byte nonce |
| `ephCPrivate` / `ephCPublic`, `nonceC` | Core ephemeral ECDH key and 32-byte nonce |
| `transcriptHash` | `SHA-256("orkestr-e2e-v1" ‖ coreId ‖ deviceId ‖ ephD ‖ nonceD ‖ ts_be64 ‖ ephC ‖ nonceC)`; both sides sign these 32 bytes (ECDSA with SHA-256, i.e. WebCrypto `sign({name:"ECDSA",hash:"SHA-256"}, key, transcriptHash)`) |
| `ecdhSharedX` | ECDH x-coordinate (WebCrypto `deriveBits(…, 256)`) |
| `hkdfSalt` | `nonceD ‖ nonceC` |
| `hkdfInfo` | UTF-8 `"orkestr-e2e-v1" ‖ coreId ‖ deviceId` |
| `kD2C`, `kC2D` | HKDF-SHA256 output 64 bytes split 32/32 |
| `clientHello`, `serverHello`, `clientFinish` | Exact JSON handshake frames (`t` discriminator, camelCase) |
| `records[]` | `{direction, dir, counter, plaintext, record}`; `record = ctr_be64 ‖ AES-256-GCM(k, iv = dir_be32 ‖ ctr_be64, aad = ctr_be64)` (ciphertext ‖ 16-byte tag). `dir` = 1 device→core (kD2C), 2 core→device (kC2D). Counters start at 0 per direction and must be strictly sequential. |

Handshake frames on the wire (each one WebSocket message, JSON):

```json
{"t":"clientHello","v":"e2e-v1","coreId":"…","deviceId":"…","ephPub":"…","nonce":"…","ts":1790000000000}
{"t":"serverHello","ephPub":"…","nonce":"…","sig":"…"}
{"t":"clientFinish","sig":"…"}
{"t":"error","code":"unknown_device|revoked|bad_signature|stale|replay|malformed|disabled"}
```

After `clientFinish` every message in both directions is a binary record whose
plaintext is one UTF-8 JSON frame of the local protocol (`auth`/`req`/`res`/`sub`/`event`).
The core sends no explicit "finished" message; if the handshake is refused it
sends an `error` frame (plain JSON) and closes the stream.
